[quote=astanir;60650118][b]Ostlandic Training[/b]
The situation on the mainland was getting better day by day. Now, with the newly trained soldiers integrated into the ranks of the Kuhaw-Astan army, they would be ready for a huge attack on the mainland.

The ships provided to Kuhaw-Astan would be integrated into the navy, which was currently serving patrol purposes only. Kuhaw-Astan knew that they couldnt yet retake the lower islands, so they would focus on the mainland for now.

[b]Operation Kauaila[/b]
The army of Kuhaw-Astan would now be standing at almost 1 million soldiers at their disposal, thanks to the newly trained soldiers and Nordiheimian mercenaries, as well as the Argossian fighting spirit. The Kuhaw-Astan command would now give the order to execute the long-planned operation Kauaila.

During this operation, the army would split roughly in half. These two halves would be named the 1st army and the 2nd army.

The 1st army would swing up north from Kuhaw-Astan territory to capture the lauqif peninsular. This would give them access to even more coastline and push the restorationists into the east. This part of the operation would go smoothly, as the restorationists had left their mainland territories almost barren in a last-ditch attempt to save the stronghold island from the UDF. This meant that the 1st army didnt have to expend much of their expensive equipment, simply brute forcing their way north and capturing the entire peninsula within one week.

The 2nd armys objectives would be far more ambitious. Their end goal was to capture the entirety of the restorationists northern territories. This may sound like a large feat on paper, but in practice the restorationist resistance would once again be minimal. Despite this, the argossians still knew that the cost of brute strength to gain such large swathes of territory would be too high to sustain. This army would instead adopt a blitzkrieg-esque strategy, making use of their new aerial capabilities and the modern technology provided by Nordiheim.

This part of the operation would begin with a combined assault against the restorationist frontline. Nordiheimian-provided tanks and armoured vehicles would roll across the battlefield, closely supported by the entirety of kuhaw-astans limited airforce. The restorationist airforce would be distracted at the stronghold island, giving the argossians an easy time in the air. These combined convoys would speed towards key road junctions, taking control of the major transport routes and subsequently creating a backup network of supplies to fuel the operation. The army would also use these key points to surround restorationist positions and close in on them. This is when the argossians would make use of the Nordiheimian drones, which would rise out positions across the encircled area. The strategy would continue across the entire northern territory, with the restorationists outdated tactics standing no match against Nordiheimian training.

The entire operation would be complete within 2 weeks. The argossians first major operation would be a resounding success.

[b]Destroying the exclave[/b]
Whilst most troops would be diverted north from the southern frontlines to take part in operation Kauaila, a small expeditionary unit comprised of Nordiheimian mercenaries and trained argossians would remain in the south, to finally crush the restorationist exclave. Their positions only continued to fail and so the exclave would come under Argossian control within days. The Argossians had now opened up a clean frontline against the isolationists, ready for battle

[b]October 30-31, 2026: The negotiations of the Doge[/b]

Following the October 26 speech by Piter Drømm and the successful elections of the communists in the City-Confederation of North Thýven (Allegedly soon to be renamed to the Peoples Confederation of North Thýven). Albus Capricorn, along with the other princes, began to see themselves increasingly sidelined for the populist rhetoric of Piter Drømm.

As a result, fearing that they would eventually be fully removed from the interim council, and fearful of the alliance that Drømm and Malben had formed over the weeks following the Northern Accords, the princes would urge Capricorn to make a formal visit with Drømm to seek guarantees of continuity.

Thus on October 30th, Albus Capricorn would meet for the first time with Piter Drømm in person under the guise of discussing the Free Republic of Knygta and Deyn, and its status in the new government. The meeting would begin easily, with Drømm accepting the letters of credence from Capricorn. However, a clear ideological divide would arise as Drømm turned the conversation to the wealthy merchant bourgeois who made up the legislature of the free republic, with Drømm noting a smaller separate people's body that had begun to rise in response to the call for constitutional conventions. 

While Capricorn would grant assurance to Drømm that the legislature was in reform, the evidence stood in contrast to Capricorn's statements, with Drømm accusing Capricorn of attempting to cling to power. 

Following the end of the meeting on October 30th, Piter Drømm would meet with Malben to discuss potentially removing the Doge via a special peoples referendum, enacting the Right of the Peoples that had been used in September to lay out the two points agreement. Malben would eagerly agree to the matter, though requesting that Drømm ensure that a successor to the Doge was chosen aforehand. It was thus agreed that a snap-election would be held in the Free Republic of Knygta and Deyn on November 11th and 12th.

Following their meeting, Capricorn would be summoned once again by Drømm on the 31st where he would inform Capricorn that he had intention to remove him from office via a people's referendum. Though Capricorn protested, his protests fell upon deaf ears, and hed be escorted out quietly by IDF officers.  Under the recommendation of Malben, Drømm would formally detain Capricorn, with his release scheduled for November 13th, thereby allowing leeway for a new head of the Free Republic to be chosen, and weakening any claim Capricorn might have to the office of the Doge.

[spoiler=[b][i]A conversation between X. Almstedt and I. Evesti[/i]

Geolocated by sensors to a private library study in Polijamsa, Gythena

31 October 2026 1:03 AM NST[/b]] 

[b]"Irja, good to meet you! Doing well so far? It's been uh... a week right? Yeah, a full week since we last met."[/b]

"I suppose so."

[b]"Still monotone as ever, huh? Well, do what you want, having go-getting business-minded automatons are also good, if a bit boring. Sometimes we might want a bit of the human touch, you know? Makes the customer feel more at ease, makes the shareholder feel more in control of their own fate."[/b]

"... The revolution has been going well, Mr. Almstedt."

[b]"Cool, cool. Go on then, tell me what's up."[/b]

"The Commonwealth armed forces are deserting in droves. It is a simple result of their wages no longer serving a purpose. Most stores no longer accept shillings, while most banks refuse to exchange the same, and so the common man is forced to accept the New Order in order to use the gold assignats. Thus, we have good reason to believe that the revolution has achieved its civilian objectives of inspiring the public to embrace us. The [i]Kommunardit[/i] have therefore informed me that they are ready and willing to take the next step. We have abolished feudalism, now we must abolish everything else and build a New Order."

[b]"That's great then. Almstedt Corporation is on the uptick these past few months too. We're feeding children in Astanir and building laboratories in Qianxun, we're loaning out bullion here in Gythena and extinguishing fires in Vespuria. So long as I can have your assurance that the Gythenan government is able and willing to cooperate for our mutual interests, then we'll be able to craft a healthy working relationship."[/b]

"We thank you for helping in the revolution, Mr. Almstedt, but you should know well enough by now. I am a communist; I believe that capitalism is undone by the dialectic, that so long as it continues to destroy the human will to survive, it will be itself destroyed and its functions seized by the proletariat. Now therefore, at the onset of total victory, it seems to me very odd to continue to work with you, especially as my followers believe that the best path forward is to the New Order that is without greed."

[b]"Capitalism makes good use of greed, but greed does not come from capitalism, Ms. Evesti. I recommend you be a bit pragmatic here. Your people are now free, but freedom without bread makes the old ways a helluva lot more attractive. It's why the revolution in Qianxun, in Sanguivallis, Astanir all decided to use some form of private industry to survive, and now you can do the same here. Eliminate free enterprise if you want, but there is something to be done that is better than irrational self-immolation. Let me into the revolution and Gythena will be fed. Let my corporation become, even if just on paper, a new organ of whatever socialist-oriented economy you're planning on creating."[/b]

"You're demanding a communist to grant you a monopoly."

[b]"Yes."[/b]

"Do you even know what socialism stands for?"

[b]"It's a system in which everything is owned by the state. Not that I'm particularly amazed by it, being a man of industry myself, since I believe a world without markets is an inefficient world. That said, Almstedt Corporation can be subsumed into the state and work candidly with its functionaries."[/b]

"Socialism is a system in which everything is owned by the worker. However, socialism is a broad thing, and many men and women throughout history have sought countervailing theories of how this may be achieved. Socialism under total state control, of course, is one of them. Some nations have sought to implement socialism without the need of a state through a network of voluntary communes, for example, though these systems were destroyed by imperialist forces, which is why socialism no longer manifests through such manner anymore."

[b]"What's your point, Ms. Evesti?"[/b]

"I want to work with you, Mr. Almstedt. Really, I do. I just fear that I am poisoning this movement by turning to the Old Order for help. The type of communism espoused by the Socialist International follows a political line that I frankly disagree with, as they believe that a nation must first transition into a state of advanced capitalism before key industries may be seized by the worker. This risks entrapping the revolution in the capitalist stage forever. The people are clothed and fed, but unequally, beneath the shadow of the Old Order."

[b]"You keep mentioning the Old Order, Ms. Evesti. I'm assuming it refers to us men of industry? It's an odd term, as though we've been organized to fight against you. The desire for private property is by no means organized, you know."[/b]

"By general principle, the defense of private property is generally mandated by self-interest, and thus unorganized. However, at the moment of the workers' revolution, the Old Order unites itself as one to destroy the coming of the new. And so, I've named it correctly. The Old Order is the long sleep of mankind. Even now we are unconscious. As I communicate with you, I hear the slumber of a hundred million half-dead souls, walking blind and astray through the heart of darkness, purposeless, waiting to misstep into the terrible freefall of the Old Order's parasitic design. We have lived to be perfected by the machine and be used and discarded for the benefit of industry and commerce. It has always been like this. Our experiences had been fabricated decades ago without our agency such that in every page in this story of our lives, the world course corrects us like a mighty river current, passing opportunistically through the path of least resistance, crashing through soil and rock, dragging us into its flow to be deposited into the depths of the unknowable ocean. Whatever grace and beauty had been known to us at the moment of creation were destroyed in the crowning of the first king. Since then, we have slept beneath the suzerains of the Old Order and are now just realizing the nightmare that had permeated for all human history. Have you seen what happens to human bodies under coma? Our muscles atrophy under the weight of the severe neglect, bones demineralize, skin sores start forming from the constant sleep, the catheters slowly poison us with infections and pneumonia. Then, we're awakened, but hollowed out. The revolution has awakened us, but we have been emptied of the things that once made us man, chained instead to the sins of an Old Order, but the revolution will rebuild us, atom by atom, tissue by tissue, until we begin again, as the New Man, in a New Order."

[b]"And the New Order is communism?"[/b]

"To label any extant movement as communism is idiotic, because communism is the distant journey in the sky. No. The New Order is the supreme necessity that must be done for the awakening of all men from the Old Order. It is the workers' revolution, the storming of the city gates and palaces, the total annihilation of the people's enemy and the bourgeoisie, the formation of the soviets, the Supreme Soviet, the end of private markets, of hoarding, the transition into industry and services, the upliftment of the peasants, the formulation of the New Man that is without the cultural inadequacies of the Old, the end of the Church and of God."

[b]"... Ms. Evesti, would you consider yourself a utilitarian?"[/b]

"A utilitarian? As in, if I would sacrifice one for many? No. Communism, by its nature, is not utilitarian. The objective of communism is the complete and utter obliteration of the Old in pursuit of the New. I am willing to sacrifice a billion lives unwilling to accept the revolution so that a thousand could build a New Order in the ashes."

[b]"In that case, what's a few compromises here and there so your little project gets its wheels oiled up and ready for the long road ahead? Almstedt Corporation is willing to provide everything you need at rates that you'll never see, not with your neighbors that currently want to destroy you. So long as you keep your state corporations in our hands, we'll do everything in our power to do right by your revolution. And if you feel like I'm screwing with you, we'll let you build up missiles so you can bomb my HQ in Stormhaven at a nifty discount."[/b]

"... But you're not doing this out of the goodness of your heart..."

[b]"Is anyone, really? Do people do good things for good alone? Perhaps, sometimes. I feel some sense of elation when I see tha face of a small street urchin brighten up after I give them a few bits of coin, but maybe that elation is because I felt myself become his master and by my own whim I've decreed he could be fed for the day. Is that goodness, or is that the will to power? Or, a better question. Does any of it matter to the public who is receiving my goodness, even if it is selfish? The fact of the matter is, Ms. Evesti, you've only succeeded in the revolution because the people were unhappy. You have grand ideas, sure, but what the people want is the base. I am not doing this out of the goodness of my heart. I am doing this because I believe there is profit to be made in a place that's currently being set alight. Growth from profit, innovation from growth, and profit from innnovation. And then I will be dead, rich and happy. But do the people care about my greedy ambitions? Of course not. What they care about is waking up in the house they've been able to buy with their own money, to drive in a car that's been almost paid for or a bike they got for cheap from a delivery app. They care about how nice it is that the price of chicken and beef is going down and that they could afford to meet with friends and family at the third places that used to be non-existent in their youth. The people turn to revolution when simplicity becomes inconvenient."[/b]

"I disagree."

[b]"I disagree with your worldview too, but let's be realistic here, Ms. Evesti. You are surrounded by enemies now. Gythena has no strong industrial base, at least relative to your neighbors, and so you will be running deficits to finance an army that produces no goods, no resources, no contribution to the happiness of your people. You say you'll be able to afford this if the nation can just collectivize now, but you damn well know that's not gonna happen, not for now, when the people only care about meeting their initial needs. So hire me. Hire me, and I will offset the costs of the revolution, and you can be better-armed for the future."[/b]

"... Hands off anything the people will consider fundamental to their way of life. Healthcare, education, services, water and electricity... your only job is to help us build a foundation."

[b]"No problem, Ms. Evesti. Anything Gythena needs. Almstedt Corporation's main goal has always been to make people happy."[/b]

"Oh shut up."

[/spoiler]

"Okay, so the duke of...whatever the f*ck." Gaberial starts before Max interupts him
